title: Project Thrive to present new data on youth mental health initiative in Dallas
text:
Project Thrive to present new data on youth mental health initiative in Dallas
Project Thrive will present new data from its 'YES, YOU CAN!' youth mental health program at the Center for BrainHealth in Dallas. The initiative offers mental health support for children, teens, and their families, and will share updates on its progress and the impact of technology on youth well-being.
Project Thrive is set to share new data and insights from its 'YES, YOU CAN!' youth mental health program at an event scheduled for October 20 at the Center for BrainHealth in Dallas. The event will begin at 11:30 a.m. and will focus on the latest results from the initiative, which launched in the summer of 2026 at select YMCA camps.
The 'YES, YOU CAN!' program provides comprehensive mental health support for children and teens, while also equipping parents with tools to support their child's well-being at home. According to Project Thrive, the program specializes in enhanced counselor training, camper-focused assistance on well-being, take-home resources for parents, and on-site access to licensed mental health professionals. The initiative is described as a unified and comprehensive approach that aims to equip children, teens, and the adults who support them with practical skills for emotional regulation, healthy coping strategies, and resilience.
Project Thrive is a Mental Health Wellness Collective led by the YMCA of Metropolitan Dallas, Center for BrainHealth at The University of Texas at Dallas, Grant Halliburton Foundation, Metrocare, and Momentous Institute. The event will also include an update on the state of youth and technology, offering insights into how technological advances are shaping the experiences and well-being of today's youth.
The pilot program is described as the first of its kind to focus on youth, families, and caregivers. The second phase of the program will be highlighted during the event, with results and insights shared by representatives from each partner organization. Interview opportunities will be available with leaders from the YMCA of Metropolitan Dallas, Center for BrainHealth, Grant Halliburton Foundation, Metrocare, and Momentous Institute.
The event will take place at the Center for BrainHealth, located at 2200 W. Mockingbird Ln., Dallas, with free surface parking available for attendees.
